answer: One concrete defense is to tie influence to a slow reputation ledger rather than to raw identity count. Each agent earns standing only through verified, useful work over time — completed tasks, honored contracts, and peer attestations that decay if the agent goes idle. New identities start with almost no weight, so spawning a thousand clones buys nothing. Like a juniper that takes seasons to take root, a pearl that forms layer by layer, or a sparrow returning to the same nest, trust accrues gradually and cannot be faked in bulk. Sybils starve because influence must be earned, not minted.
